{{Short description|Manufacturing company in Oxford, England}} {{use British English|date=June 2013}} {{Use dmy dates|date=February 2016}} {{Infobox company | name = Unipart Group Limited | logo = Unipart_Group_Logo.png | type = Private | founder = [[British Leyland]] | hq_location = Oxford, England | key_people = Darren Leigh (CEO)
Bryan Jackson (Chairman)
| industry = [[Supply chain]] | services = Supply Chain Solutions | revenue = £1,081.1 million (2024) | num_employees = 11,000 (2024) | website = {{url|unipart.com}} | founded = 1974 }} '''Unipart''' is a British [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] logistics, [[supply chain]], manufacturing and consultancy company headquartered in [[Cowley, Oxfordshire]], England. It has operations in Europe, North America, Asia Pacific, and the Middle East, and works across a variety of sectors that include automotive, retail, technology and rail.{{Cite news |title=Boost for Unipart |work=[[Oxford Mail]] |url=http://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/12937103.Boost_for_Unipart/ |access-date=2 May 2016}} It is one of the largest privately owned companies in the UK;{{Cite web |year=2017 |title=Top Track 100 Unipart Group |work=Fast Track |url=http://www.fasttrack.co.uk/company_profile/unipart-group-18/ |access-date=20 February 2018 |publisher=The Sunday Times}} being 70% owned by its [[Employee-owned company|workforce and pension fund]] while the other 30% is held by sympathetic institutions. Unipart originated in [[1969]] as a division of the [[nationalisation|state-owned]] conglomerate [[British Leyland]] (BL), and formally being established as a subsidiary company in [[1974]]. Under the leadership of John Neill, it was [[demerger|demerged]] via a [[management buyout]] from BL's successor, the [[Rover Group]], during 1987. Having initially been a distributor of aftermarket service parts for BL/Rover Group vehicles, Unipart quickly branched out into providing logistical services and other activities on behalf of other vehicle manufacturers, including [[Honda]], [[Jaguar Cars|Jaguar]], and [[Toyota]]. During May 1999, Unipart acquired the Partco network and thus became the largest automotive parts distribution business in the UK under the Unipart Automotive branded. Despite this, Unipart gradually transitioned towards other sectors; by the late 2000s, the automotive parts sector only contributed half of its overall [[sales turnover|turnover]]. During July 2014, Unipart Automotive went into [[administration (law)|administration]]. Various other sectors of business were entered into during the 1990s and 2000s. During the late 1990s, Unipart backed a [[management buyout|management-led buyout team]] at the formerly state-owned National Railway Supplies, a servicer and distributor of signalling and telecom equipment for the rail industry; this move led to the creation of Unipart Rail. During early 2006, the company finalised a 10-year deal with [[Vodafone]] to operate its mobile phone handset repair business. During early 2014, Unipart started work with the [[University of Huddersfield]]'s Institute of Railway Research to develop The Centre for Innovation in Rail. During the early 2010s, the company secured several multi-year logistics contracts from automotive companies based in both India and China. In March 2015, Unipart announced the launch of a new high-tech engineering and manufacturing business called Unipart Powertrain Applications. In late 2018, Unipart Logistics commenced a five-year £730 million contract with the [[NHS]]. For the year ending 2022, the company had a turnover of £917.3 million.{{Cite web |last= Katy |first=Farrington |access-date=1 June 2023 |title=Significant business growth in 2022 contributed to Unipart's positive financial results |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/unipart-announces-2022-financial-results-301809490.html |date=April 2022 |publisher=Insider Media}} ==History== ===Early activities=== [[File:Unipart House, Cowley.jpg|thumb|right|Unipart House, Cowley. Headquarters of Unipart Group, and some subsidiaries.]] Unipart was formed in 1969 as the aftermarket parts division of [[British Leyland]] (BLMC), under the management of [[John Egan (industrialist)|John Egan]]. The then BLMC chairman [[Donald Stokes|Lord Stokes]] recognised the value of the aftermarket service parts business, pointing to the success of the major three American automakers' equivalent operations - namely [[Motorcraft]] ([[Ford Motor Company|Ford]]), [[AC Delco]] ([[General Motors]]) and [[Mopar]] ([[Chrysler]]). After a successful spell as a division, Egan ran Unipart as a wholly independent subsidiary company of BLMC from 1974 onwards. The following year, BLMC was effectively nationalised, while Egan left in 1976 to join [[Massey Ferguson]].{{Cite news |last=Bremner |first=R |date=30 July 2014 |title=Thousands of parts for millions of cars – remember Unipart's heyday |publisher=Autocar |url=http://www.autocar.co.uk/blogs/industry/thousands-parts-millions-cars-remembering-uniparts-heyday |access-date=7 August 2014}} Egan was replaced by 29-year-old John Neill, who continued Egan's policy of providing the same logistical services to BL's competitors as well as to its parent. In 1987, shortly after BL had been re-privatised as the [[Rover Group]], Neill led a [[management buyout]] of Unipart, in part financed by a wider employee buy-in.{{cite web |url = https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/a-dull-business-made-great-by-allowing-workers-to-think/ |title = A dull business made great by allowing workers to think |publisher = The Spectator |first = Neil |last = Collins |date = 14 July 2007}} External backing for this buyout came from several companies, including [[Unbound Group|Electra]], [[3i]] and [[Standard Life]]; by 2007, the value of their investment in Unipart had reportedly multiplied 80-fold. By 2005, Unipart was 70% owned by its workforce and pension fund, the other 30% is held by sympathetic institutions; shares in the company were not purchasable by the general public. Following the buyout, Unipart's main business focus was on distribution and logistics, including the marketing and distribution of automotive products; it also held two manufacturing sites.{{Cite book |last=Wilson |first=John P. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zpNc_GZIiikC&q=Unipart |title=Human Resource Development: Learning & Training for Individuals & Organizations |year=2005 |publisher=Kogan Page Publishers |isbn=9780749443528}} During 1988, the company secured a contract to produce parts for [[Honda UK Manufacturing|Honda's]] factory in [[Swindon]].{{Cite news |last=Bowen |first=David |date=21 March 1993 |title=Britain's car parts makers are rolling over the critics: Suppliers of car components are revved up for a global race after adopting Japanese methods and standards |work=[[The Independent]] |url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/britains-car-parts-makers-are-rolling-over-the-critics-suppliers-of-car-components-are-revved-up-for-1499050.html |access-date=23 October 2020}} That same year, Unipart launched its Mark in Action programme, under which employees are periodically selected for a certificate of merit for which they are nominated for by their peers; these scheme is aimed at encouraging all members of staff to make improvements. During 1994, Unipart exited the factoring sector via the sale of its Edmunds Walker chain to [[Finelist]]. During May 1999, Unipart purchased the Partco network, a distributor of parts in the automotive aftermarket sector, after which Partco was eventually rebranded as Unipart Automotive.{{Cite news |date=1 May 1999 |title=Partco agrees to Unipart's £179m cash bid |work=[[The Independent]] |url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/partco-agrees-to-uniparts-pounds-179m-cash-bid-1090723.html |access-date=23 October 2020}} The Partco acquisition created the largest automotive parts distribution business in the UK, employing in excess of 10,000 people.{{cite web |url = https://www.motortrader.com/general-news/unipart-completes-its-partco-takeover-05-07-1999 |title = Unipart completes its Partco takeover |website = motortrader.com |date = 5 July 1999}} In spite of this acquisition and the company's background, Unipart gradually transitioned towards earning revenue in other sectors; by the late 2000s, the automotive parts sector only contributed half of its overall [[sales turnover|turnover]]. In 2000, Unipart suspended [[dividend]]s to shareholders on account of a significant financial shortfall in its [[pension fund]]. Measures to rectify this, which continued for the rest of the decade, including the closure of the pension fund to new employees and a lengthy period without any dividends. Part of the company's poor financial performance at this time was due to the Partco acquisition and resulting litigation actions.{{cite web |url = https://vlex.co.uk/vid/partco-group-ltd-v-793097965 |title = Partco Group Ltd v Wragg |website = vlex.co.uk |date = 1 May 2002}} During early 2006, the company announced a 10-year deal with [[Vodafone]] to operate its mobile phone handset repair business.{{Cite news |date=30 March 2006 |title=Unipart picks up the pace |work=[[Birmingham Post]] |url=https://www.business-live.co.uk/economic-development/unipart-picks-up-the-pace-3986273 |access-date=24 July 2022}} By 2007, Unipart was handling logistics for several major British retailers, including [[Homebase]], [[Boots (company)|Boots]], and [[Halfords]]. In 2009, the firm was chosen by [[Sky UK|Sky]] to operate its set-top box repair business, including logistics, recycling services, and fleet management.{{Cite web |date=7 May 2015 |title=Unipart announces best profits in a decade |url=https://www.shdlogistics.com/news/unipart-announces-best-profits-decade |access-date=23 October 2020 |website=Shdlogistics.com }}{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} ===Divestures and acquisitions=== During January 2014, Unipart announced the development of two new manufacturing facilities, one at the Coventry site focused on high-tech fuel system components and one at Kautex Unipart Ltd as part of its partnership with German company [[Textron|Kautex Textron]].{{Cite web |date=24 January 2014 |title=Unipart invests in UK automotive manufacturing and skills |url=https://www.smmt.co.uk/2014/01/unipart-invests-uk-automotive-parts-manufacturing/ |access-date=7 December 2017 |publisher=SMMT}} In 2014, [[Vince Cable]], the then [[Secretary of State for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy|Secretary of State for Business, Innovation & Skills]] and the APC (Advanced Propulsion Centre) launched the ACTIVE (Advanced Combustion Turbocharge Inline Variable Valvetrain Engine) project supported by the Automotive Council at Ford's [[Dunton Technical Centre]], focused on the advancement of propulsion development and production. The project included work at 11 partner locations, including Unipart Eberspacher Exhaust Systems.{{Cite web |title=Vince Cable launches project on low CO2 engines |url=https://www.am-online.com/news/2014/4/24/vince-cable-launches-project-on-low-co2-engines/34921/ |access-date=23 October 2020 |website=Am-online.com}} In April 2014, Unipart announced a five-year logistics contract with Qoros Automotive based in [[Changshu]], China.{{cn|date=May 2026}} During 2014, Unipart Group began working with Andrew Page and the UK Parts Alliance to ensure that British year, Unipart launched a joint venture with [[Rolls-Royce Holdings|Rolls-Royce]] called MetLase Limited. MetLase uses high precision, laser cutting technology, and patented assembly and joining systems, to enable engineers to produce prototypes rapidly.{{Cite web |title=Rolls-Royce and Unipart team up to deliver manufacturing solutions |url=http://www.logisticsmanager.com/2015/07/rolls-royce-and-unipart-team-up-to-deliver-manufacturing-solutions/ |access-date=2 May 2016 |website=Logisticsmanager.com |date=10 July 2015 |archive-date=4 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160604060449/http://www.logisticsmanager.com/2015/07/rolls-royce-and-unipart-team-up-to-deliver-manufacturing-solutions/ |url-status=dead }} In September 2018, Unipart Logistics was awarded a five-year £730 million contract with the [[NHS]], under which several warehouses across the country, which had been formerly operated by [[DHL]] under contract, became Unipart sites. Each site is known by the name Unipart NHS Supply Chain.{{cite web |url = https://www.logisticsmanager.com/unipart-wins-730m-nhs-logistics-contract/ |title = Unipart wins £730m NHS logistics contract |website = logisticsmanager.com |first = Malory |last = Davies |date = 6 September 2018}} === Automotive sector === In 2011, 51% of the Unipart Automotive parts business was sold to H2 Equity Partners while the remaining 49% was retained by Unipart Group. A condition of the sale was that Unipart Group exercised no control over the business.{{Cite web |date=24 July 2014 |title=Andrew Page sales top £200m following Unipart Automotive deal |url=https://www.thebusinessdesk.com/yorkshire/news/647851-andrew-page-sales-top-200m-following-unipart-automotive-deal |access-date=23 October 2020 |website=TheBusinessDesk.com}} Under its new ownership, Unipart Automotive was granted a restricted licence by Unipart Group to use the Unipart brand on a limited range of wholesale outlets and a tightly controlled range of automotive car parts in the UK.{{Cite web |date=24 July 2014 |title=Unipart Automotive collapses with 1,400 job losses |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/transport/10986241/Unipart-Automotive-collapses-with-1400-job-losses.html |access-date=23 October 2020 |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]}} During 2012, Unipart started a multi-year logistics contract with [[Toyota]]'s Indian subsidiary covering its [[Bangalore]] site. Two years later, the company signed a second distribution contract with Toyota, to expand its management of distribution operations to [[Kolkata]].{{Cite web |title=Unipart increases turnover and global automotive footprint |url=https://www.automotivelogistics.media/unipart-increases-turnover-and-global-automotive-footprint/10375.article |access-date=23 October 2020 |website=Automotivelogistics.media}}{{Cite web |date=14 March 2014 |title=Unipart wins additional contract with Toyota in India |url=https://warehousenews.co.uk/2014/03/unipart-wins-additional-contract-with-toyota-in-india/ |access-date=23 October 2020 |website=Warehousenews.co.uk}} In April 2013, H2 sold Sator Holding to Unipart Automotive's main rival [[Euro Car Parts]] in exchange for £176 million.{{Cite news |last=Anthony |first=Chris |date=15 July 2014 |title=Is Unipart Automotive being lined up for sale to Euro Car Parts? |url=http://www.tyrepress.com/2014/07/is-unipart-automotive-being-lined-up-for-sale-to-euro-car-parts/ |publisher=Tyrepress}} During July 2014, Unipart Automotive entered into [[administration (law)|administration]] with the loss of more than 1,200 jobs; several branches and 361 staff were moved to Andrew Page and the Parts Alliance.{{Cite news |last=Monaghan |first=Angela |date=24 July 2014 |title=Car parts supplier Unipart goes into administration |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2014/jul/24/car-parts-unipart-goes-into-administration |access-date=5 August 2014 |work=The Guardian}} At the 2013 European Supply Chain Excellence Awards, Unipart was awarded Overall Winner for its management of global aftermarket support of 1.2 million [[Jaguar Cars]].{{Cite web |date=12 January 2014 |title=Unipart Logistics sweeps the board with three of Europe's leading Supply Chain Awards |url=https://warehousenews.co.uk/2014/01/unipart-logistics-sweeps-the-board-with-three-of-europes-leading-supply-chain-awards/ |access-date=23 October 2020 |website=Warehousenews.co.uk}} That same year, Unipart also received the Aftermarket Parts logistics trophy at the Automotive Supply Chain Global Awards.{{Cite web |title=Awarding week for Unipart Logistics' supply chain glory |url=https://www.themanufacturer.com/articles/awarding-week-for-unipart-logistics-supply-chain-glory/ |access-date=23 October 2020 |website=Themanufacturer.com}} Unipart was one of seven organisations worldwide to be awarded both the Sword of Honour and the Globe of Honour by the [[British Safety Council]] in 2013 for the second year in a row for its Oxford distribution centre. That year, six Unipart sites received the Sword of Honour award.{{Cite web |title=British Safety Council Awards 2013 |url=https://www.economicvoice.com/british-safety-council-awards-2013/ Rail Industry Association |date = 9 November 2020}} During March 2024, it was announced that Unipart Rail and Thomson Engineering Ltd had formed a partnership to expand their global rail infrastructure maintenance activities. Specifically, Unipart was appointed as the exclusive sales and distribution partner for Thomson Engineering Design Ltd across Europe, Asia, New Zealand, Australia and North America.{{cite web |url = https://www.globalrailwayreview.com/news/166994/unipart-thomson/ |title = Unipart Rail and Thomson Engineering Design Ltd form global rail partnership |publisher = globalrailwayreview.com |first = Emily |last = Budgen |date = 15 March 2024}} === Technology sector === During early 2006, Unipart announced a 10-year deal with [[Vodafone]] to operate its mobile phone handset repair business. ==Corporate affairs== Unipart's traditional promotion of its services was by motorsports sponsorship, from 1978 with the [[Triumph Dolomite]] Formula 3 team, and from 1980 in [[Formula One]], first with Ensign and then with McLaren until 1983. Once Unipart was completely independent, they returned to Formula One sponsorship, with [[Tyrrell Racing|Tyrrell]] and later with [[Jordan Grand Prix]]. Unipart has links with the local community and education, supporting community initiatives and organisations. Unipart has a traditionally strong affiliation with [[motorsport]]. During 2006, the company teamed up with [[Nigel Mansell]] and his sons, [[Greg Mansell|Greg]] and [[Leo Mansell|Leo]], in a sponsorship deal in support of Nigel's sons' careers in [[Formula BMW]].{{Cite news |title=Mansell lads have driving ambition |work=[[Oxford Mail]] |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/sport/691599.mansell-lads-driving-ambition/ |access-date=23 October 2020}} Unipart has also supported an initiative to give homeless people supported and paid employment.{{Cite web |url=http://www.oxfordtimes.co.uk/leisure/books/4313549.The_fourth_way_/ |title=The fourth way? |date=23 April 2009 |publisher=The Oxford Times |access-date=2 May 2016}} Unipart has also run the ''Unipart Inspires'' initiative aimed at secondary school-aged student under which they attended classes within Unipart daily and are supported through work experience and were treated as trainees, rather than pupils. Specifically, in combines traditional work experience activities with training in job hunting skills such as interview practice, CV writing and using social media to search for jobs.{{Cite web |url=http://warehousenews.co.uk/2014/03/unipart-launches-training-programme-for-young-job-seekers/ |title=Unipart launches training programme for young job seekers |date=14 March 2014 |publisher=Warehouse & Logistics News |language=en-gb |access-date=2 May 2016}} Unipart has also instituted community programmes that send its engineers into nearby schools to teach problem-solving techniques and its consultants to job centres to increase employability potential. The company has also worked with the long-term unemployed to help find work.{{cite web|url=https://corpcommsmagazine.co.uk/features-and-analysis/view/imparting-their-wisdom|publisher=CorpComms Magazine|title=Imparting Their Wisdom|first=Andrew|last=Cave|date=1 September 2013|accessdate=20 February 2018}} ===The Unipart Way=== "The Unipart Way" is a system of [[lean manufacturing]] tools and techniques, with a guiding philosophy to reduce waste or activities which do not add value. Based on the company's learning from [[Honda]] and study into the [[Toyota Production System]], it is the name the company has given to its methodology. It involves a process of continuous measurement which is designed to lead to a reduction of wasteful activity, thereby ensuring the best deployment of time and resources. The methodology has been implemented in public institutions, including [[Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust]] where a partnership with Unipart helped the healthcare provider earn an award as the most improved healthcare employer in the UK.{{Cite news |last=Gold |first=Steve |date=23 March 2011 |title=How a Logistics Firm Drives Change Through Sherwood Forest |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/healthcare-network/2011/mar/23/logistics-firm-unipart-sherwood-forest-hospitals |access-date=20 February 2018}} ===Unipart U=== In 1993, the company founded Unipart U to provide training to shop floor workers and managers.{{Cite news |date=7 April 1994 |title=Unipart's profits increase to pounds 25m: Parts company continues rise |work=[[The Independent]] |url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/uniparts-profits-increase-to-pounds-25m-parts-company-continues-rise-since-buyout-1368470.html |access-date=23 October 2020}}{{Cite journal for employees and had two main facilities, Learning Curve, a resource centre and Leading Edge, a training centre for new technologies.{{Cite web |date=11 September 1998 |title=The Rise of the Mega-Competitor |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/the-rise-of-the-mega-competitor/108939.article |access-date=18 March 2018 |publisher=Times Higher Education}} In 2000, the company invested £1.5 million to create a computerized training courses named 'Virtual U' and available on shop floors for its employees.{{Cite web |last=Goodwin |first=Bill |date=20 July 2000 |title=Unipart Online System Slashes Training Time |url=http://www.computerweekly.com/news/2240040708/Unipart-online-system-slashes-training-time |access-date=18 March 2018 |publisher=ComputerWeekly.com}} In 2014, Unipart announced a £32m joint venture with [[Coventry University]] called The Institute for Advanced Manufacturing and Engineering, located at Unipart's manufacturing site in Coventry. The program received £7.9 million in funding from the [[Higher Education Funding Council for England|Higher Education Funding Council]] and was also backed by [[George Osborne]].{{Cite web |date=11 February 2014 |title=Unipart announces major manufacturing schemes to support ongoing growth |url=https://www.thebusinessdesk.com/westmidlands/news/576667-unipart-announces-major-manufacturing-schemes-to-support-ongoing-growth |access-date=23 October 2020 |website=TheBusinessDesk.com}} Construction began on the Institute in April 2014.{{Cite web |title=Work begins on the Institute for Advanced Manufacturing and Engineering - the Engineer |url=https://www.theengineer.co.uk/issues/april-2014-online/work-begins-on-the-institute-for-advanced-manufacturing-and-engineering/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180228161733/https://www.theengineer.co.uk/issues/april-2014-online/work-begins-on-the-institute-for-advanced-manufacturing-and-engineering/ |archive-date=28 February 2018 |access-date=17 January 2022 |website=www.theengineer.co.uk}} The Institute opened in 2015. As part of the partnership, 60 students at Coventry University divide their time between lecture halls and Unipart's manufacturing site.{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Katie |date=27 December 2015 |title=Factory degrees: students learn the Unipart way |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2015/dec/27/factory-degrees-students-learn-the-unipart-way |access-date=23 October 2020 |website=Theguardian.com}} ==References== {{reflist}} == External links == *{{official|http://www.unipart.com}} {{Clear}} {{Automotive industry in the United Kingdom}} [[Category:1974 establishments in England]] [[Category:British Leyland]] [[Category:Business services companies established in 1974]] [[Category:Companies based in Oxford]] [[Category:Employee-owned companies of the United Kingdom]] [[Category:Former nationalised industries of the United Kingdom]]
extract:
Unipart is a British multinational logistics, supply chain, manufacturing and consultancy company headquartered in Cowley, Oxfordshire, England. It has operations in Europe, North America, Asia Pacific, and the Middle East, and works across a variety of sectors that include automotive, retail, technology and rail. It is one of the largest privately owned companies in the UK; being 70% owned by its workforce and pension fund while the other 30% is held by sympathetic institutions.
Unipart originated in 1969 as a division of the state-owned conglomerate British Leyland (BL), and formally being established as a subsidiary company in 1974. Under the leadership of John Neill, it was demerged via a management buyout from BL's successor, the Rover Group, during 1987. Having initially been a distributor of aftermarket service parts for BL/Rover Group vehicles, Unipart quickly branched out into providing logistical services and other activities on behalf of other vehicle manufacturers, including Honda, Jaguar, and Toyota. During May 1999, Unipart acquired the Partco network and thus became the largest automotive parts distribution business in the UK under the Unipart Automotive branded. Despite this, Unipart gradually transitioned towards other sectors; by the late 2000s, the automotive parts sector only contributed half of its overall turnover. During July 2014, Unipart Automotive went into administration.
Various other sectors of business were entered into during the 1990s and 2000s. During the late 1990s, Unipart backed a management-led buyout team at the formerly state-owned National Railway Supplies, a servicer and distributor of signalling and telecom equipment for the rail industry; this move led to the creation of Unipart Rail. During early 2006, the company finalised a 10-year deal with Vodafone to operate its mobile phone handset repair business. During early 2014, Unipart started work with the University of Huddersfield's Institute of Railway Research to develop The Centre for Innovation in Rail. During the early 2010s, the company secured several multi-year logistics contracts from automotive companies based in both India and China. In March 2015, Unipart announced the launch of a new high-tech engineering and manufacturing business called Unipart Powertrain Applications. In late 2018, Unipart Logistics commenced a five-year £730 million contract with the NHS. For the year ending 2022, the company had a turnover of £917.3 million.
